subject: phy
title: Gravitation
syllabus: The universal law of gravitation; acceleration due to gravity and its variation with altitude and depth; Kepler's laws of planetary motion; gravitational potential energy; gravitational potential; escape velocity; motion of a satellite, orbital velocity, time period and energy of satellite.

body: Forces add as vectors (superposition). Equal masses placed symmetrically around a point give zero field there.
Field of a uniform shell is zero inside; outside, a sphere acts as if all its mass sat at the centre.
Gravity is ~10^{39} times weaker than the electric force between an electron and a proton.

cards.t: g at height, depth and on other planets
body: g is largest at the surface; it falls going up AND going down.
Other planet: g ∝ \f{M}{R^{2}} = \f{4}{3}πGρR. Pendulum period T = 2π√{\f{L}{g}} changes with g, not with the bob's mass.
If the earth shrank with the same mass, angular momentum stays the same: day length ∝ R^{2}.
U is zero at infinity and negative everywhere else. Energy to send a body to infinity from the surface = \f{GMm}{R} = mgR.
Raising a body to height h: ΔU = mgR(1 − \f{R}{R + h}) — equals mgh only when h ≪ R.
v_{e} ∝ √{\f{M}{R}} ∝ R√{ρ}; it does not depend on the mass of the body or the direction of launch.

check.q: KE to escape from the surface :

body: Kepler: orbits are ellipses; equal areas in equal times (angular momentum constant, central force); T^{2} ∝ r^{3}.
Close to the surface: v = √{gR} ≈ 7.9 km/s, T ≈ 84 min, and T = √{\f{3π}{Gρ}} depends only on the density.
Geostationary: T = 24 h, r ≈ 42 000 km, above the equator. Moving to a bigger orbit needs energy \f{GMm}{2}(\f{1}{r_{1}} − \f{1}{r_{2}}).

traps: Height from the SURFACE vs distance from the CENTRE: r = R + h.
g falls both above and below the surface.
Total energy of an orbit is negative; KE = −E.
Escape speed does not depend on the launch angle or the body's mass.
T^{2} ∝ r^{3} only for the same central mass.
Energy to escape is mgR, not ½mgR.

pyq.q: A light planet is revolving around a massive star in a circular orbit of radius R with a period of revolution T. If the force of attraction between planet and star is proportional to R^{−3/2} then choose the correct option :
sol: Gravity supplies the centripetal force: mω^{2}R ∝ R^{−3/2} → ω^{2} ∝ R^{−5/2}.

pyq.q: A 90 kg body placed at 2R distance from surface of earth experiences gravitational pull of : (R = Radius of earth, g = 10 m s^{−2})
sol: Distance from the centre = R + 2R = 3R → force falls by 3^{2} = 9.

pyq.q: A metal wire of uniform mass density having length L and mass M is bent to form a semicircular arc and a particle of mass m is placed at the centre of the arc. The gravitational force on the particle by the wire is :
sol: Radius r = \f{L}{π}, mass per length λ = \f{M}{L}.
For a semicircle the sideways parts cancel; the field at the centre is \f{2Gλ}{r}.

When released, they interact only through gravitational force and collide after a time T = 4 seconds. If the sides of the triangle are increased to length 2a and also the masses of the spheres are made 2m, then they will collide after ______ seconds.
sol: Only G, m and a can set the time: by dimensions t ∝ √{\f{a^{3}}{Gm}}.

pyq.q: Net gravitational force at the center of a square is found to be F_{1} when four particles having mass M, 2M, 3M and 4M are placed at the four corners of the square (M bottom-left, 2M bottom-right, 3M top-right, 4M top-left) and it is F_{2} when the positions of 3M and 4M are interchanged. The ratio \f{F_{1}}{F_{2}} is \f{α}{√{5}}. The value of α is ______.
sol: Each mass pulls the centre-particle along its diagonal with force ∝ its mass (same distance).
F_{1}: diagonals M↔3M and 2M↔4M → net 2M and 2M at right angles → 2√{2}M.

pyq.q: Four identical particles of mass m are kept at the four corners of a square. If the gravitational force exerted on one of the masses by the other masses is (\f{2√{2} + 1}{32})\f{Gm^{2}}{L^{2}}, the length of the sides of the square is
sol: On one corner (side a): two neighbours give \f{Gm^{2}}{a^{2}} each at 90° → √{2}\f{Gm^{2}}{a^{2}}; the far corner adds \f{Gm^{2}}{2a^{2}} along the same diagonal.

pyq.q: If R is the radius of the earth and the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is g = π^{2} m/s^{2}, then the length of the second's pendulum at a height h = 2R from the surface of earth will be,:
sol: A second's pendulum has T = 2 s → L = \f{gT^{2}}{4π^{2}}.

If the radius of earth is reduced to three-fourth of its present value without change in its mass then value of duration of the day of earth will be ______ hours 30 minutes.
sol: No outside torque → angular momentum Iω is constant; I = \f{2}{5}MR^{2}.

pyq.q: Acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is 'g'. If the diameter of earth is reduced to one third of its original value and mass remains unchanged, then the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is ______ g.

The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is g. If the diameter of earth reduces to half of its original value and mass remains constant, then acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth would be :
sol: g ∝ \f{1}{R^{2}} → halving R makes g four times.

Reason (R): The mass of the pendulum remains unchanged at Earth and the other planet. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: g on the planet = \f{G(4M)}{(2R)^{2}} = g → same period: A is true.
R is true, but T = 2π√{L/g} does not depend on the bob's mass — R does not explain A.

pyq.q: Assertion A: The kinetic energy needed to project a body of mass m from earth surface to infinity is \f{1}{2}mgR, where R is the radius of earth. Reason R: The maximum potential energy of a body is zero when it is projected to infinity from earth surface.
sol: Energy needed = 0 − (−\f{GMm}{R}) = \f{GMm}{R} = mgR, not ½mgR: A is false.
Potential energy −\f{GMm}{r} rises to its maximum 0 at infinity: R is true.

sol: Falling from infinity: ½mv^{2} = mgR → v = √{2gR} = √{2 × 9.8 × 6.4 × 10^{6}} = 11.2 km/s.
